title: Weights & Measures — DeepSeek V3, a Model Built Around Its Chips
show_notes:
DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report — DeepSeek-AI (2024)

What did DeepSeek V3's famous five-and-a-half-million-dollar figure actually measure, and what engineering made it possible? Jack and Molly unpack the December 2024 report behind the open-weight model: a mixture of experts that uses 37 billion of its 671 billion parameters per token, the chip-to-chip traffic that design creates on Nvidia H800s, its load-balancing trick and compressed attention cache, and what later models kept and dropped. The policy thread asks what happens when a rule turns on one technical number, from US chip export controls to the EU AI Act's compute threshold.

Notes: benchmark comparisons are DeepSeek's own runs. The $5.576M figure assumes a $2-per-GPU-hour rental rate and, per the paper, covers only the official training run, excluding prior research and ablations. The EU-threshold comparison uses Epoch AI's compute estimate, not a DeepSeek figure.

Jack and Molly are AI-generated hosts; research and script by Oggy.

Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.19437 · https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.04434 · https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09343 · https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.19737
